architectural_fidelity.reason: Room is clearly recognizable: same beige/neutral walls, same ceiling height, same window position and size with blinds, same camera angle and viewpoint, same beige carpet, no invented walls.

furniture_removal.reason: All original furniture completely removed—bed, desk setup, nightstands, office chair, speakers, and all accessories are gone with no ghost outlines or remnants visible.

style_commitment.reason: COVAJAPANDI should be a distinctive coastal-Japandi fusion style; this render shows generic minimalist staging with a basic platform bed, dark credenza, and minimal accessories—lacks the committed aesthetic identity expected from a named style designation.

editorial_density.reason: Severely under-styled: only 5 items total (bed, credenza, small plant, wicker pouf, one pillow)—no wall art, no layered textiles beyond one throw, single light source, no surface vignettes, no lived-in editorial details that Collov demonstrates.

photorealism.reason: Lighting is soft and somewhat flat with reduced shadow definition; credenza appears slightly CGI-rendered with simplified textures; overall acceptable but noticeably less photographic than Collov's crisp material definition and dynamic lighting.

designer_preference_reason: Collov delivers publication-ready editorial staging with complete style commitment and layered details, while Cova presents an under-furnished, generic minimalist space that clients would find incomplete.
what_cova_does_better: Perfect furniture removal with no artifacts
Maintains exact architectural integrity of the original space
what_collov_does_better: Editorial-level decor density with multiple textile layers, art, plants, and accessories
Committed, identifiable style execution with cohesive design language
Superior photorealism with dynamic lighting and crisp material textures
Multiple light sources creating dimensional depth
Styled surface vignettes and lived-in details
specific_fixes_if_failing: Add wall art above bed (minimum 2-piece gallery or statement piece)
Layer textiles: add decorative pillows (4-5), throw blanket, textured bedding set
Include nightstands with table lamps for layered lighting
Add area rug to define sleeping zone and add warmth
Style surfaces with books, decorative objects, and organic elements
Introduce more plants (2-3 additional) for organic warmth
Define COVAJAPANDI aesthetic clearly: combine coastal textures (jute, linen, light wood) with Japandi principles (low furniture, natural materials, negative space with intention)
Add reading chair or floor cushion seating element
Include window treatments beyond basic blinds
Improve lighting rendering for more dimensional shadows and material depth
